nodes.name: Continuous cathodic electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The films were cathodically deposited from a 0.1 M solution (total metal basis) prepared by mixing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (Alfa Aesar) and FeCl2·4H2O (Sigma-Aldrich) in a 100:0, 95:5, 90:10, or 85:15 (mol Ni:mol Fe) ratio in 18.2 MΩ cm water. Continuous depositions from the 5, 10, and 15% Fe solutions resulted in 8, 16, and 23% Fe in the films. The deposition solution was sparged with N2 for 20 min prior to film deposition. All films were deposited at a cathodic current density of -25 mA cm^{-2}. Continuously deposited films were subjected to reducing potentials for 10 s.
nodes.source_text: 2.2. Film Deposition... Continuous depositions from the 5, 10, and 15% Fe solutions resulted in 8, 16, and 23% Fe in the films.

nodes.name: Pulsed cathodic electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Pulse-deposited films from 5% Fe solution resulted in 15% Fe in the films. Pulse-deposited films were subjected to sequential 2 s cathodic current pulses at 25 mA cm^{-2}. Following each pulse, the solution was stirred for 10 s to ensure homogeneity of the deposition solution prior to the next pulse. All pulse-deposited films were synthesized using five cycles unless otherwise noted.

nodes.name: Film rinsing
nodes.procedure: All films were briefly dipped into ultrapure water to remove residual metal ions prior to electrochemical testing.

nodes.characterization_summary: PDF patterns best simulated by brucite-like β-Ni(OH)₂ fragments 1-3 layers thick; NiO_xH_y matches bilayer hydroxide domain (16×16×2 unit cells, ~5 nm); Ni₈₅Fe₁₅O_xH_y best represented by single-sheet domain (11×11×1 unit cells).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PDF patterns for Ni_{(1-z)}Fe_zO_xH_y films are best simulated by model structures consisting of brucite-like β-Ni(OH)₂ fragments 1 to 3 layers in thickness... The NiO_xH_y film matches well with a bilayer hydroxide domain. The Ni₈₅Fe₁₅O_xH_y film is best represented by a smaller single-sheet domain.

properties.peaks_observed: Multiple peaks around 1.5-3.5 Å and beyond

nodes.characterization_summary: Films cycle between as-deposited, oxidized, and reduced states with minimal loss of intrasheet coherence; oxidation state significantly affects intralayer metal-oxygen bond distance (Ni(Fe)-O: 2.1→1.9 Å; Ni(Fe)-Ni(Fe): 3.1→2.9 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Films can be cycled between as-deposited, oxidized, and reduced states, with minimal loss of intrasheet coherence... the first shell Ni(Fe)-O shortens from 2.1 to 1.9 Å upon oxidation and is accompanied by a corresponding decrease in the di-μ-oxo-linked Ni(Fe)-Ni(Fe) distance from 3.1 to 2.9 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: M-O bond length decreases with Fe content in reduced state due to Fe^{3+} substitution; oxidized Ni(Fe)OOH shows increasing M-O and M-O-M bond lengths with Fe content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The addition of Fe into Ni(OH)_2 decreases the average M-O bond length, consistent with the substitution of Fe^{3+} onto Ni^{2+} sites in the structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO_xH_y domain coherence length decreases with increasing deposition pulses: 5-10 pulses fit bilayer structures, 15-25 pulses fit single sheet structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For example, the NiO_xH_y film prepared with five pulses is best described by a 16×16×2 bilayer model, while the film prepared with 25 pulses is best modeled with a 6×6×1 single layer.

properties.description: Plot of residual R-factor (green axis) and best fit model (dashed line) versus domain dimension in unit cells

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO_xH_y film with 5 pulses shows domain heterogeneity: optimal fit uses linear combination including ~30% 5×5 domains and mixture of mono-, bi-, and trilayer 16×16 domains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nearly 30% contribution from the 5×5 model in the optimized fit indicates that smaller domains contribute significantly to the overall pattern.
